NURS6200.title: Nurs Sensitive Hlth Outcom
NURS6200.description: Conceptual, philosophical, theoretical, epistemological, methodological, and feasibility issues central to health outcomes research are examined. The concept of health outcomes and related health and social policies from the perspective of nursing practices are analyzed and critiqued. The impacts of nursing practices on health outcomes at individual, family, community, and population levels will be discussed, analyzed and critiqued.

NURS6300.title: Doctoral Seminar
NURS6300.description: The goal of the doctoral seminar is for students and faculty to share the findings from their research, engage in scholarly debate, and foster scholarship. The seminar will facilitate proposed and ongoing research between and among doctoral students, faculty members, and other keystakeholders. Focus is on the critical examination of the research process in nursing, health service delivery, and policy decision-making with an emphasis on maintaining the links between the research problem, theory, and research methods. Consideration is given to both quantitative and qualitative research approaches, designs, and data collection and analysis.  Knowledge translation as a core component of research design will be discussed. Strategies for critically analyzing research studies and for utilizing findings are examined.

NURS6800.title: Directed Doctoral Study
NURS6800.description: This course offers doctoral students the opportunity to undertake further study in a specific topic of interest that is not covered by regular course offerings. The student will be supervised by a faculty member who is competent in the area of interest. Regular meetings between the student and the supervising faculty member will be held. The method of evaluation will be contracted by the student and supervising faculty member.

NURS6820.title: Doctoral Reading Course
NURS6820.description: This course offers doctoral students the opportunity to undertake further study in a specific topic of interest that is not covered by regular course offerings. The student will be supervised by a faculty member who is competent in the area of interest. Regular meetings between the student and the supervising faculty member will be held. The method of evaluation will be contracted by the student and supervising faculty member.

NURS8100.title: Anat. and Phyl I
NURS8100.description:
Provides students with an understanding of the fundamental principles of human anatomy and physiology.  This course will enable students to describe and explain the gross anatomy and histology of the human body.  Students will study the functions of the organs and systems of the body focusing in basic cellular physiology.  Learners will study the functions of the organs and systems of the body as they relate to nursing practice.  The course will also explore the integration of functions within the body.
Additional lab requirement 2 hours per week

NURS8101.title: Anat. and Phyl II
NURS8101.description:
Provides students with an understanding of the fundamental principles of human anatomy and physiology.  This course will enable students to describe and explain the gross anatomy and histology of the human body.  Students will study the functions of the organs and systems of the body focusing in basic cellular physiology.  Learners will study the functions of the organs and systems of the body as they relate to nursing practice.  The course will also explore the integration of functions within the body.
Additional lab requirement 2 hours per week

NURS8102.title: Intro. to Psy. Nurs.
NURS8102.description: An overview of psychological theory is used to introduce students to the biopsychosocial factors that influence human behaviour. Students develop an understanding of personality development, the biology of behaviour, sensation and perception, learning and other concepts involved in the social behaviour of humans.

NURS8103.title: Intro. to Soc. for Nurs.
NURS8103.description: Provides students with an overview of general concepts of sociology and how they relate to the structure and function of communities in circumpolar environments. The impact of the historical relationship between Inuit and non-Inuit people on Inuit social structures, processes, and the health of families and communities are explored.

NURS8104.title: Acad. Writ.
NURS8104.description: The course will explore a variety of issues in academic writing such as style, argument, format and the presentation of information. The course is designed to prepare students to write academic papers. Frequent written exercises will be required.

NURS8105.title: Intro. to BioChem
NURS8105.description: Topics discussed include the structure, biosynthesis and functions of biologically important compounds, enzymes, control of metabolism, genetic engineering and nutrition. Medical aspects are stressed.

NURS8106.title: Hlth. Sc. MICI
NURS8106.description: An introduction to microbiology and infectious diseases only for healthcare professionals. It includes a study of the structure and physiology of microorganisms, the ways microorganisms cause disease in man and the way they affect human's wellbeing.

NURS8110.title: Teaching and Learning
NURS8110.description: Students will critically analyze and integrate the teaching-coaching domain of nursing practice through examination of the developmental, sociocultural and motivational conditions that affect teaching and learning.  Principles and theories of learning are used to develop health education strategies for diverse populations.  Students will develop communication and teaching skills.

NURS8111.title: Foundations of Nurs Practice
NURS8111.description: Ethical, professional, legal concepts and theories guiding professional nursing practice are examined.  Professional identity, collaboration, comportment, and reasoning related to nursing practices are developed.  Theories and frameworks are used to investigate health and social care constructs and the impact of hierarchal structures on individual, communal and global health.

NURS8115.title: Clinical Integration I
NURS8115.description: Integration of foundational nursing skills and practices, such as health history and assessment, safety, infection control, communication and relational inquiry occurs in clinical application settings. Students use multiple learning modalities to master fundamentals of nursing practice.

NURS8210.title: Health & Healing
NURS8210.description: Fundamentals of health and disease patterns, the role of genetics, developmental biology and environment are explored. Cellular mechanisms, inflammatory and infectious responses and cellular biology of cancer are investigated. Diagnosis and therapeutic concepts including preventative therapies and pharmacological and non-pharmacological interventions with consideration of age and cultural variations are introduced.

NURS8211.title: Community and Mental Hlt
NURS8211.description: The structure and relationships in our existence are fundamental to the development of human potential and nursing practice. Community concepts for a healthy society in the context of northern communities will be introduced.  Mental, spiritual, and physical health concerns that impact on health and social well-being in communities will be explored.

NURS8212.title: Contemporary Issues Hlth
NURS8212.description: The changing patterns of health care delivery and increasing complexity in all practice environments are examined. The nurses’ role requires exploration of clients’ unique biopsychosocial spiritual and cultural needs and advocacy of health choices and decisions. Ethical decision making and reasoning related to nursing practices are developed.

NURS8215.title: Clinical Integration
NURS8215.description: Through clinical application (using simulation & clinical experiential learning) students will integrate nursing process, critical thinking, relational practice and evidence-informed decision making in caring for clients with acute and chronic alterations in health to achieve optimal functioning.

NURS8220.title: Health & Healing II
NURS8220.description: Integrating knowledge of disease, diagnosis and person-centred management is key to successful nursing practice. Specific disease processes related to body systems are described and mechanisms of therapeutic options for management are evaluated. Evidence to support use of pharmacological, non-pharmacological, alternative and complimentary treatments is evaluated.

NURS8221.title: Nursing Research
NURS8221.description: Examines the methods used to generate, apply and evaluate knowledge in nursing and health care focusing on the basic processes of quantitative, qualitative and epidemiological research. The emphasis is on analysis, synthesis and evaluation of research and the implications for theory and evidence-informed nursing practice. Collaboration with inter-professional research teams is described.

NURS8222.title: Found Clinical Nurs Practice
NURS8222.description: Collaborating with adults across the life course who experience acute and/or chronic physical or mental illness requires a focus on preventative and curative care strategies. Utilization of evidence and application of nursing and interprofessional collaborative care and informed decision-making is examined within the context of person, family, and society.

NURS8225.title: Clinical Integration III
NURS8225.description: Using simulation and clinical experiential learning students apply knowledge related to caring for clients with acute, episodic illnesses from birth to death.  Interprofessional practice and evaluation of the impact of collaborative care will be a focus.

NURS8310.title: Professional Formation
NURS8310.description: Leadership is integral to the practice of every nurse. Examining and applying leadership theories and behaviours enable effective practices to be evaluated. The nursing role in conflict resolution, crisis intervention and therapeutic communication to manage complex situations using multiple perspectives is examined.

NURS8311.title: Nursing Conc. Age
NURS8311.description: Guided by the principles of Primary Health Care students focus on the psychosocial, cultural, cognitive, and spiritual health of adults and on nursing practices that promote health in adults at specific developmental stages.  Issues of determinants of health are specifically addressed.  Strategies to promote healthy aging at the individual, family, and community level are explored.

NURS8312.title: Nursing Concepts Family
NURS8312.description: Focuses on the concepts of health related to childbearing families including assessment during pregnancy, birth and post-partum.  Approaches to perinatal care and the role of midwifery in northern communities are explored.  Theories and concepts in caring for the family as client are utilized

NURS8315.title: Clinical Integration IV
NURS8315.description: Population health, family and perinatal theoretical concepts and evidence are utilized in a variety of practice settings.  Family health assessments across various family life stages including focused fetal/newborn/child and parental care in dynamic inter-professional settings enable students to apply theory to practice.

NURS8320.title: Nurs. Concepts Child/Adl/YAdlt
NURS8320.description: Principles of Primary Health Care are applied to health promotion, risk reduction, disease prevention, and common health problems experienced by infants, children, young adults, and their families in rural and remote settings.  Concepts of healthy development, illness, and disability, related to the health of the child, adolescent, young adult and family unit are explored.

NURS8321.title: Comm. and Population Health
NURS8321.description: Students focus on integration of community, public health theory and nursing practice as it applies to primary health care within a population health context.  The philosophical basis, roles, settings and functions of community health nursing will be examined and used to explore evidence-informed nursing care delivery to persons, families and populations in community settings.

NURS8325.title: CI V: Child/Adol/Young Adlts
NURS8325.description: Students participate in the care of children, adolescents, young adults and families along a continuum from prevention to specialized care.  Through project work students develop an understanding of health equity using principles of primary health care and social determinants of health to positively influence the health profiles of the pediatric population living in the North.

NURS8410.title: Rel. Prac. and Adv. Cln.
NURS8410.description: Students engage in relational inquiry, clinical reasoning and multiple ways of knowing related to health and social care. Evaluation of evidence in the context of person-centred care forms the basis for reflective practice that promotes health and wellness and supports management of complex situations.

NURS8411.title: Prf. Frm. Nurs and Soc. Rsp
NURS8411.description: Collaborating with and across professions, theoretical frameworks are critiqued and applied to gain insight into the nursing role that influences policies and practices in health care. Evaluation of the processes that influence and support change, as well as system inertia, will assist in developing strategies to improve health for society

NURS8415.title: Rel. Prc. and Adv. Cln. Rsn
NURS8415.description: Students engage in a broad range of clinical, research, and theoretical learning experiences under the supervision of faculty members or clinical preceptors/facilitators to complete a project relevant to nursing practice. Through these experiences, students develop an understanding of the complexity of the integrated nursing role and its application across diverse healthcare and community settings.

NURS8425.title: Tra. Prc. North I
NURS8425.description: Students synthesize their nursing knowledge and refine entry-to practice competencies through integration of theory and practice in concentrated clinical mentorship programs.  Through intensive engagement in application of evidence-informed and person-centered care, students are able to develop and refine skills to enhance future nursing practice that is specific to northern nursing.

NUTR3000.title: Introduction to Nutrition
NUTR3000.description: A study of the principles of nutrition, including the digestion, absorption, and metabolism of nutrients. Content is applicable to humans and animals with a focus on domestic and companion animal species.  Functions of protein, lipids, carbohydrates, vitamins, and minerals are studied.

NUTR3001.title: Applied Animal Nutrition
NUTR3001.description: Classification and characteristics of feedstuff and regulations governing their use are described. Methodology for evaluating the relative merits of typical feedstuffs is discussed. The principles of nutrition are applied in the formulation of rations for monogastric, avian, and ruminant species.

NUTR3002.title: Fish Nutrition
NUTR3002.description: Nutrients required by finfish, shellfish, crustaceans, and molluscs are discussed in context with current and future sources of these nutrients. Digestive physiology and specific feeding problems of aquatic species are addressed. Diet formulations and feeding strategies for maintenance, growth, and reproductive performance of fish are covered.

OCCU2000.title: Occupation & Daily Life
OCCU2000.description: This introductory course for students in any field of study is designed to explore the meaning of occupation in everyday life. Typically, the term “occupation” refers to categories of paid work. This course will explore a broader understanding of occupation as a framework for daily living; namely what we need to do, want to do, or have to do daily, and over time. Students will be exposed to a broad range of literature on occupation, including personal and environmental factors that influence, and are influenced by, occupation. Students will gain a deeper understanding of occupation as the foundation of everyday life through a range of perspectives and experiential activities.

OCCU3500.title: Human Occu Across Lifespan
OCCU3500.description: Designed for students from any discipline, this course builds on basic concepts in occupational science. We explore how human development from infancy through late adulthood shapes participation, performance and meaning in occupations. Far beyond employment, 'occupation' means those purposeful activities that occupy time, energy, and attention.

OCCU4500.title: Social Sanctioning in OCCU
OCCU4500.description: This course will cover the key concepts and debates in occupational science, with focus on the social structures which lead to the binary labelling of occupations as "sanctioned" and "non-sanctioned." Students will gain in-depth understanding of the way society shapes the values and statuses associated with occupations, where available through a comparative, cross-cultural perspective. This will be achieved through a comprehensive, interdisciplinary study of literature relevant to occupations.

OCCU5009.title: Fieldwork & Practice Int.
OCCU5009.description: Integrating knowledge and skills from the current term, students practice applying theory, frames of reference, occupational analysis and assessment, and clinical reasoning through implementation of a practice process involving human interactions. Through direct application in various mediums and contexts, students will enhance their ability to engage in therapeutic encounters with supervision and feedback from preceptors (licensed occupational therapists). Students will demonstrate skills and professional behaviour for safe and respectful practice. Students will use the fieldwork evaluation tool(s) used nationally in occupational therapy to engage in critical analyses of their own progress.

OCCU5013.title: Foundations of OT I
OCCU5013.description: This course establishes foundational knowledge for occupational therapy practice, examining relevant theories, practice models and frames of reference used in the profession. The concept of occupation, its applicability and its limitations are introduced, along with its historical context. Principles of activity analysis and occupational analysis are introduced, leading to exploration of the principles of assessment, a vital component of professional practice. The strengths and limitations of assessment approaches are critically examined.

OCCU5014.title: Professional Practice I
OCCU5014.description: This course is designed to begin preparing students for practice in a regulated profession. It introduces Competencies for Occupational Therapists in Canada. Processes of practice and processes of reasoning used in occupational therapy are a key focus. Professional requirements are emphasized, such as scope of practice, confidentiality, ethical decision-making, boundaries, effective communication and team work. The course fosters skills for engaging with clients, including consent, interviewing, and goal-setting and documentation. Learners will be encouraged to integrate knowledge and skills gained from across courses in this term.

OCCU5016.title: Physical Hlth Practice in OT I
OCCU5016.description: This course introduces learners to physical health conditions and how these affect occupational participation. Lectures and labs will focus on occupational therapy processes of practice including assessment, intervention, and documentation. Emphasis will be on developing foundational skills for therapeutic practice with people experiencing musculoskeletal and other physical health issues. Learners will be expected to integrate learning from courses across this term.

OCCU5018.title: Lifespan, Dev & Occupation
OCCU5018.description: This course explores the development of the person through the lifespan and explores implications for occupational participation. It draws on theory and evidence from interdisciplinary fields (including occupational science) to explore how humans develop socially, psychologically, physically, neurologically, cognitively, emotionally, relationally, and spiritually. It explores a range of human differences embodied within and across cultures.

OCCU5019.title: Fieldwork I
OCCU5019.description: Integrating knowledge and skills from the previous and current terms, students practice applying theory, frames of reference, occupational analysis and assessment, and clinical reasoning through implementation of a practice process involving human interactions. Through direct application in various mediums and contexts, students will enhance their ability to engage in therapeutic encounters with supervision and feedback from preceptors (licensed occupational therapists). Students will demonstrate skills and professional behaviour for safe and respectful practice. Students will use the fieldwork evaluation tool(s) used nationally in occupational therapy to engage in critical analyses of their own progress.

OCCU5021.title: Mental Health Practice in OT I
OCCU5021.description: This course introduces learners to occupational therapy practice with individuals, families and communities emphasizing primary promotion of mental health and evidence informed approaches for responding to mental illness. Lectures will focus on common mental health concerns and conditions, assessment processes, and occupational therapy interventions for mental health practice. Critical analysis of health care systems, stigma and ableism will build skills for professional reflexivity. Labs will focus on assessment, intervention and documentation, applying processes of practice and building practice skills. Integrating knowledge and skills across courses this term is expected.

OCCU5022.title: Neurotherapeutics I
OCCU5022.description: Drawing on the reasoning and practice skills and the knowledge developed in previous and concurrent courses, this course will introduce students to the neurological aspects of occupational therapy practice. Applying knowledge across the practice process will be emphasized. Lectures will build on learning from OCCU 5014 and OCCU 5018 to address neurological conditions, assessments and interventions. In labs, hands-on practice with assessments, interventions and documentation will foster skills for working with people who experience neurological occupational issues. Integrating knowledge and skills across courses this term is expected.

OCCU5023.title: Foundations of OT II
OCCU5023.description: Building on OCCU 5013 and OCCU 5014, this course focuses on strengthening familiarity with and application of occupational therapy theories, practice models and frames of reference. Practice processes and developing clinical reasoning are central, with an emphasis on application in multiple practice contexts. Social determinants of health, universal design, and accessibility are flagged as key to working in communities and institutions. Drawing on critical disability perspectives and theories from around the globe, the course cultivates critical reflexivity, skills for questioning received knowledge.

OCCU5024.title: Neuroscience for OT
OCCU5024.description: This course provides students with the foundational neuroscience knowledge and application of human neuroanatomy and neurophysiology concepts for occupational therapy practice. The focus is on neurophysiology of the central and peripheral nervous systems. Emphasis will be placed on functional neuroscience pertaining to common neurological conditions and cognition.

OCCU5025.title: Research I
OCCU5025.description: This course introduces students to a range of research paradigms and methodologies, including quantitative and qualitative, as well as broad considerations for the credibility of evidence. Students will learn about research ethics, study designs, sampling and data analysis, as well as critical appraisal skills to examine the quality of evidence. The integration of research and other forms of evidence to inform practice will be emphasized.

OCCU5026.title: Social Inequities and OT
OCCU5026.description: This course explores the ways occupation and occupational therapy practice are shaped by social privilege and oppression. Students will learn to critically analyse how intersecting axes of oppression and privilege shape experiences, values, and assumptions, while also affecting occupational opportunities and barriers. Approaches to anti-oppressive practice will be introduced.

OCCU5029.title: Fieldwork II
OCCU5029.description: In this field education course, students focus on the broad scope of occupational therapy practice, building capacity for occupational participation with individuals, groups and communities. Though experiences and expectations will vary by site, students begin to develop professional identity and an applied understanding of scope of practice. Students describe and justify their clinical reasoning through the full process of occupational therapy practice, demonstrating skills and professional behaviour for safe and respectful practice. Under the supervision of licensed occupational therapists, students receive feedback and frequent coaching. Students engage in critically reflexive practice.

OCCU5035.title: Research II
OCCU5035.description: This course builds on foundational learning from OCCU 5025 (Research I) for students to develop skills to conduct a research project. Students will identify an occupation-related topic or choose one from topics submitted by faculty. Most students (Stream A) will conduct in-depth, critical reviews of existing evidence. There is an option for students to apply to pursue empirical research (Stream B). Research initiated in this course will be pursued in OCCU 6025 (Research III), together comprising the major project work for the Master of Science (Occupational Therapy) program.

OCCU5043.title: Prog Eval for Occptnl Therapst
OCCU5043.description:
The course develops knowledge and skills in program evaluation through critical appraisal of key issues and challenges facing occupational therapy practitioners. The course provides an overview of the key phases and issues in program evaluation.
TECHNOLOGY & SOFTWARE: Consult http://www.dal.ca/ilo for current technologies.

OCCU5500.title: Social Sanctioning of OCCU
OCCU5500.description: This course will cover the key concepts and debates in occupational science, with focus on the social structures which lead to the binary labelling of occupations as “sanctioned” and “non-sanctioned.” Students will gain in-depth understanding of the way society shapes the values and statuses associated with occupations, where available through a comparative, cross-cultural perspective. This will be achieved through a comprehensive, interdisciplinary study of literature relevant to occupations.

OCCU6013.title: Advanced Practice Issues
OCCU6013.description:
This course builds skills in critical analysis, evidence-based professional reasoning, presentation, and synthesis of previous knowledge into current practice. Using current issues in health and occupational therapy practice, the required exercises of reflecting, reasoning, determining a personal perspective and developing a plan of action strengthens current and life-long learning patterns. Integration seminars will be used to support the acquisition of these outcomes.
TECHNOLOGY: Consult http://www.dal.ca/ilo for current technology requirements

OCCU6016.title: Phys Hlth Practice in OT II
OCCU6016.description: This course strengthens occupational therapy processes of practice with individuals experiencing physical health conditions. Building on OCCU 5016, it emphasizes more complex conditions, assessments and interventions. Lectures will focus on physical health conditions, assessments, and intervention approaches. Labs will focus on applying clinical reasoning and developing practice skills for assessment, intervention, and documentation. Students will integrate learning from courses across this term through case-based activities.

OCCU6019.title: Fieldwork III
OCCU6019.description: In this field education course, students focus on developing competence, confidence and skill in working with individuals, communities, and/or organizations to respond to complex occupation-related challenges. Though fieldwork experiences and expectations will vary by site, students develop a clear professional identity, and gain skill in detailing and justifying their clinical reasoning, and implementing the full process of occupational therapy practice. Critical reflexivity becomes a routine part of practice. Students will demonstrate skills and professional behaviour for safe and respectful practice. Under the supervision of licensed occupational therapists, students receive feedback and periodic or occasional coaching.

OCCU6021.title: Mental Hlth Practice in OT II
OCCU6021.description: This course strengthens occupational therapy processes of practice, working with families, communities and systems to support and promote mental health and wellbeing. It addresses the ways mental health intersects with social conditions (such as poverty, housing precarity, addictions, criminalization), affecting occupational participation. Primary prevention of mental illness and addiction will be a key focus, along with evidence-informed therapeutic approaches. Ethical standards and ethical decision-making will be emphasized, as well as processes for navigating mental health and addictions care within and beyond the formal healthcare system. Labs will focus on applying clinical reasoning and practice skills for assessment, intervention and documentation.

termClasses.location: Carleton COLLABORATIVE HEALTH EDUC BLDG C170

OCCU6022.title: Neuro and Cognitive Rehab II
OCCU6022.description: Building on learning from OCCU 5022, this course will strengthen student reasoning, skills and processes of practice for working therapeutically with individuals who experience challenges due to neurological conditions. Lectures and labs will focus on therapeutic approaches in neurological rehabilitation and cognitive rehabilitation. The course addresses complex conditions, focusing on conditions, assessments, interventions and documentation. Labs will promote hands-on practice skills. Learners will be expected to integrate knowledge and skills across courses this term.

OCCU6023.title: Resisting Colonialism in OT
OCCU6023.description: This course will critically examine the colonial underpinnings of occupational therapy, encouraging learners to explore and appreciate multiple perspectives on knowing and doing. Starting from historical and contemporary colonial practices in Canada and Mi’kma’ki, and impacts on health, well-being and occupation, it will explore the colonial biases built into the foundations of the profession (theories, models, practices). Building on local and global anti-colonial approaches to occupational therapy, it will specifically attend to Indigenous epistemologies and the need to take responsibility for transforming practice processes. Students will be introduced to approaches to challenge colonialism within themselves and the profession.

OCCU6024.title: Incl Comm, Tech & Design
OCCU6024.description: This course focuses on inclusion to optimize community belonging and occupational participation for all people. With a focus on rights, relationships and belonging as well as access, students learn practices and policies intended to support universal design and/or inclusion in multiple contexts. Students learn to assess for inclusion, as well as how to employ design, technology and community approaches to enhance inclusion and occupational participation. Students reflexively critique the limitations of inclusion, as well as the strengths and limitations of technologies.

OCCU6025.title: Research III
OCCU6025.description: Building on work conducted in OCCU 5035 (Research II) students (Stream A) will continue to critically analyze and interpret research evidence on their selected topic, producing a written literature review. Students who have been approved to conduct empirical research (Stream B) will complete data collection and analysis, writing up their research. All students will present their analyses at a final capstone research conference.

OCCU6029.title: Fieldwork IV
OCCU6029.description: During this final fieldwork learning experience students focus on consolidating and refining core competencies, critically reflecting on practice, and seeking new challenges with minimal guidance from preceptors. Though fieldwork experiences and expectations will vary by site, students become independent in working with individuals, groups, organizations and/or communities, implementing the full process of occupational therapy practice. By the completion of this course, students demonstrate confidence and consistency in using sound clinical reasoning and making skilled judgments showing readiness for entry-level professional practice. Under the supervision of licensed occupational therapists, students will demonstrate skills and professional behaviour for safe and respectful practice. Students implement critical thinking and critical reflexivity in practice, advocating and acting to enhance equity in occupational participation.

OCCU6222.title: Fieldwork IV
OCCU6222.description: The course consists of eight weeks of full-time fieldwork learning under the supervision of one or more occupational therapists who provide periodic or occasional coaching, within Canada or internationally, or with off-site occupational therapy preceptors in Atlantic Canada. During this final fieldwork learning experience, with minimal guidance from preceptors, students will gain experience in implementing selected occupational therapy practice processes and theoretical models in a range of urban, rural, or remote locations. Students become independent in working with individual, groups, and organizational clients, and will develop a clear professional identity and learn to describe and justify professional reasoning through the process of occupational therapy practice. By completion of this course, students will demonstrate clinical confidence and consistency in making sound professional decisions and judgments in preparation for entering professional practice.

OCCU9001.title: Thesis
OCCU9001.description: The thesis requires original research at the master's level.  Basic or applied research using qualitative or quantitative methodologies will be conducted as appropriate.  Thesis supervision by distance will involve email, telephone, post, teleconference or other communication as appropriate.TECHNOLOGY: Consult http://www.dal.ca/ilo for current technology requirements

OCCU9002.title: Thesis
OCCU9002.description: The thesis requires original research at the master's level related to occupation. Basic or applied research may use qualitative or quantitative methodologies as appropriate. Thesis supervision will be provided by a faculty member associated with the School of Occupational Therapy and a thesis committee, as per Faculty of Graduate Studies Regulations.  Thesis Supervision is typically offered by distance and may involve email, telephone, teleconference, videoconference, or other communication as appropriate. As part of the thesis process, the student will develop and defend a thesis proposal, complete ethics applications as appropriate, and complete all steps of the research process. Thesis defense normally occurs via distance, but may be attended in person, and follows Faculty of Graduate Studies Regulations.

OCEA1001.title: Conversat w/ Ocean Scientst I
OCEA1001.description: Students engage with working ocean scientists about their research, its relevance, and how to communicate science to different audiences. In addition to regular writing exercises that include journaling, blogging, and lab reporting, students compose a research paper and follow it through the process of submission and peer-review for an in-class journal.

OCEA1002.title: Conversat w/ Ocean Scientst II
OCEA1002.description: Students engage with working ocean scientists about their research, its relevance, and how to communicate science to different audiences. In addition to regular writing exercises that include journaling, blogging, and lab reporting, students compose a research paper and follow it through the process of submission and peer-review for an in-class journal.

OCEA2001.title: The Blue Planet I
OCEA2001.description: This course provides a general survey of oceanography. It is designed to develop an understanding of the ocean and of the science of oceanography. Students learn about the geological, chemical, physical and biological processes at work in the sea.

OCEA2002.title: The Blue Planet II
OCEA2002.description: This course provides a general survey of biological oceanography. Students learn about marine biology and marine ecosystems. Consideration is also given to human impacts.

OCEA2020.title: Tools and Concepts in Ocean Sc
OCEA2020.description: Students gain practical insights into oceanographic concepts introduced in OCEA 2001.03/2002.03 through lab exercises. Labs focus on navigation and position, instruments and calibration, ocean optics and acoustics, water movement, and basic marine chemistry. Labs involve data acquisition and analyses to develop quantitative skills. Students will become familiar with the 'R' programming language.

OCEA2021.title: Tools & Concept in Ocea Sci II
OCEA2021.description: Students gain practical insights into oceanographic concepts introduced in OCEA 2001/2002 through lab exercises. Labs focus on particle dynamics and life in the ocean and involve data acquisition and analysis to develop quantitative skills. At the end of the course, students observe a mesocosm to synthesize concepts from both OCEA 2020.03 and OCEA 2021.03. Students will continue to use the 'R' programming language.

OCEA2800.title: Climate Change
OCEA2800.description: See course description for PHYC 2800.03 in the Physics and Atmospheric Science section of this calendar.

OCEA3001.title: Intro to Physical Oceanography
OCEA3001.description: This course introduces Ocean Physics, focusing on issues of interest to undergraduates in ocean-related disciplines. The approach is to bind facts together with ideas, often starting with thought experiments and proceeding to simple mathematical models.

OCEA3002.title: Intro to Chemical Oceanography
OCEA3002.description: This course provides students with a basic understanding of the composition of seawater and the processes that leads to this composition. This understanding is both qualitative and quantitative through the use of thermodynamic, kinetic and box models to describe the balances that produce the observed chemical distributions.

OCEA3003.title: Intro to Field Oceanography
OCEA3003.description: This course explores interrelationships between living organisms in the sea and the ocean environment. Biological processes are introduced in the context of the physical and chemical oceanography. The emphasis is on sea-going field work on day trips in local marine waters and hands-on laboratory investigation.

OCEA3004.title: The Last Billion Years
OCEA3004.description: This course examines major events in Earth history. The geological and geochemical evidence will be described, and the hypothesized causes of the events will be examined. The goal of this course is to develop an understanding of the functioning of the earth/ocean/atmosphere system, how it has reacted to perturbations in the past and how it will react to current perturbations in the future.

OCEA3270.title: The Solid Earth
OCEA3270.description: This course aims to understand the structures and dynamics of the Solid Earth system from the surface to the inner core and from the ocean to the continent. Topics covered will include the internal structure of the Earth, plate tectonics, earthquakes, seismology, gravity, magnetic field, heat flow, and mantle convection.

OCEA3420.title: Geochem of Aqua Environment
OCEA3420.description: This course is an introduction to the governing principles and processes of aquatic geochemistry. Specific topics will include physical chemistry of natural waters, kinetics of geochemical reactions, the hydrologic cycle, the carbonate system and pH, redox reactions, weathering and mineral-solution equilibria, controls on the composition of rainwater, rivers, and oceans.

OCEA4000.title: Oceans and Global Change
OCEA4000.description: This course examines the role and response of the Oceans to global change, including alterations in currents and circulation, increases in sea level and storm surges, changes in ocean chemistry, modification to the types and patterns of sediment deposition, alterations in the abundances and distributions of organisms, and overall productivity. The course will discuss means of predicting these changes and their effects.

OCEA4110.title: Geological Oceanography
OCEA4110.description: This course provides a broad survey of geology and geophysics as they apply to the oceans.  The course content covers methods and observations with quantitative applications to an understanding of marine geophysical and geological processes.  The topics covered include the origin of ocean basins, plate tectonics, heat flow, gravity, and magnetics (1/3 of the course); patterns and processes of sediment transport and deposition, and the paleoceanographic reconstruction of past climates (2/3 of the course).

OCEA4120.title: Physical Oceanography
OCEA4120.description: This course introduces undergraduate students to the physical properties and dynamics of the oceans. Topics range from global circulation down to the small scales of turbulence. Fact and theory are blended throughout.  Quantitative problem solving is emphasized in assignments.

OCEA4130.title: Chemical Oceanography
OCEA4130.description: This course covers the major and minor constituents of sea water, the controls on its chemical composition, nutrient cycling, gas exchange and the influence of the oceans on atmospheric chemistry. Other topics included are chemical tracers, and radiochemical dating methods, stable isotope studies, chemical speciation and chemical models of sea water.

OCEA4140.title: Biological Oceanography
OCEA4140.description: The goal is to describe how physical, chemical and biological processes interact to determine the species composition, biogeochemical activities, and trophic structure of marine communities. Outstanding problems currently facing biological oceanographers and earth systems scientists are discussed, as are current attempts and methodologies to address them.

OCEA4201.title: Honours Research - Part 1
OCEA4201.description: This course is required for students enrolled in the Concentrated Honours in Ocean Sciences, and certain streams of the Combined Honours in Oceanography program. It consists of a research project under the supervision of a faculty member, and should include an original component in oceanography. Students are required to participate in weekly meetings of the class and make a presentation (oral or poster) at the annual CDOGS meeting in March.

OCEA4202.title: Honours Research - Part II
OCEA4202.description: This course is required for students enrolled in the Concentrated Honours in Ocean Sciences, and certain streams of the Combined Honours in Oceanography program. It consists of a research project under the supervision of a faculty member, and should include an original component in oceanography. Students are required to participate in weekly meetings of the class and make a presentation (oral or poster) at the annual CDOGS meeting in March.

OCEA4210.title: Time Series Analysis
OCEA4210.description: See course description for STAT 4390.03 in the Statistics section of this calendar.

OCEA4220.title: Numerical Modelling
OCEA4220.description: This course discusses numerical modelling techniques for simulating atmospheric and oceanic circulations. Material includes: review of governing equations; finite difference, finite element, and spectral methods; Eulerian, semi-implicit and semi-Lagrangian time integration techniques; accuracy and stability analyses; data assimilation and ensemble prediction methods; and boundary treatment for ocean models.

OCEA4230.title: Biology of Phytoplankton
OCEA4230.description: This is an upper-division course on the phytoplankton in the context of their evolutionary history and ecological diversity. It has an emphasis on their adaptations and acclimation to different environments and their role in food webs and biogeochemical cycling.

OCEA4301.title: Special Topics in Ocean Scienc
OCEA4301.description: This course provides upper level undergraduate students with the opportunity to study an area of Ocean Science that is not offered through the existing curriculum. Students consult with a faculty member to arrange the topic of study and together develop course proposal. The course proposal must be approved by the course coordinator before the student is permitted to register.

OCEA4302.title: Independent Res. in Ocean Scie
OCEA4302.description: Students in their 3rd or 4th year of study conduct supervised, independent research in Ocean Science. The student and a faculty supervisor together develop a course outline, with a proposal for original research and the method of evaluation, including a formal research paper. The course outline must be approved by the course coordinator before the student is permitted to register. The course coordinator is the Chair of the Curriculum Committee or designate.

OCEA4311.title: Fluid Dynamics I
OCEA4311.description: An introduction to the theory of fluid dynamics, with some emphasis on geophysically important aspects. Contents: tensor mathematics, flow kinematics, equations of motion, viscous flow, potential flow, convection, turbulence, and basic aerodynamics. Occasional reference will be made to current research topics, especially those in Physical Oceanography.

OCEA4331.title: Hist of Marine Sciences
OCEA4331.description: In this course, we will trace the history of marine sciences from the ancients to the 20th century. Topics may include ancient cosmologies, voyages of discovery, ocean circulation, and a range of scientific perspectives and technological developments that have shaped human understanding of the oceans.

OCEA4360.title: Sea Ice
OCEA4360.description: This course is an advanced undergraduate course that will provide an overview of the physics of sea ice, notably those aspects which relate importantly to oceanography. Topics will include polar oceanography; sea ice composition, growth, mechanics and dynamics; ice features including polynyas, leads, the marginal ice zone, and landfast ice; spatio-temporal variability and trends in sea ice; observing and modelling sea ice; Indigenous perspectives on sea ice; and biogeochemistry of sea ice.

OCEA4370.title: Deep Sea Biology
OCEA4370.description: We focus on the biology of organisms inhabiting the deep sea: physiological adaptations to the physicochemical and geological environment; spatial and temporal distributions of biological assemblages; and regulatory factors of these assemblages, such as currents, food availability, reproduction and recruitment. Also, we delve into unique habitats, such as hydrothermal vents.

OCEA4401.title: Marine Management I
OCEA4401.description: This course exposes students with a marine science background to the increasing need for marine scientists and ocean managers and policy makers to work collaboratively to address the interdisciplinary nature of the problems confronting the world's oceans. This course is restricted to 4th year students with a marine science background.

ORAL5000.description: This course is offered during the 1st year, consists of 14 hours of lectures and 36 hours of dissection and serves as an overview of the anatomy of the chest, thoracic cavity, arm and iliac crest areas of the pelvis. Emphasis will focus on anatomical structures and adjacencies as they relate to deformities, injuries and other pathological processes of the head and neck.

ORAL5060.description: This course is presented to residents over a two-year period, twice during the 4 years of their program. This component of the course must be completed by December 15 of the final year of the program.

PHDP8000.title: Doctoral Comprehensive Reqmt
PHDP8000.description: Following completion of course work, students will register in the Doctoral Comprehensive Requirement while they prepare for, and until they have passed, the Comprehensive Examination.

PATH3000.title: Introduction to Pathology
PATH3000.description: This course provides a general introduction into the science concerned with the basis of disease. The primary focus of the course is to highlight the basic concepts that underlie disease processes. These concepts are illustrated through a range of topics including: immunopathology, neoplasia, genetic disorder, neuropathology, hematopathology and cardiovascular pathologies.

PATH4035.title: Human Genetics
PATH4035.description: For science students with special interest in human genetics. Topics include errors of metabolism, human development, transmission genetics, DNA structure, gene function, mutation and chromosomal alterations, population genetics, genetics of immunity and cancer, genetic technology in medicine, and ethical and social issues related to medical genetics.

PATH4100.title: Critical Thnkg Neuropathology
PATH4100.description: This course focuses on breakthroughs in understanding human brain function. You will learn about the inspirations and acidents that lead to seminal discoveries. You wil be ale to understand the context of these breakthroughs. You will learn to ask better questions about the process of basic and applied research.

termClasses.location: Carleton COLLABORATIVE HEALTH EDUC BLDG C266

PATH4100.location: Carleton COLLABORATIVE HEALTH EDUC BLDG C266

PATH5000.title: General Pathology
PATH5000.description: This course covers basic systems and processes in pathology.

PATH5013.title: Biochem of Clinical Disorders
PATH5013.description: This course is an introduction to the pathophysiology of disease. It provides the clinical and biochemical background to disease groups and system disorders and the laboratory approach to their diagnosis. Topics include cardiovascular, renal, gastrointestinal and hepatobiliary disorders, in addition to acid base, carbohydrate, lipid and amio acid disorders; endocrine and rheumatological diseases, as well as tumor markers and toxicology, blood and immune abnormalities.

PATH5035.title: Human Genetics
PATH5035.description: Topics include inborn errors of metabolism, human development, transmission genetics, DNA structure, gene function, mutation and chromosomal alterations, population genetics, genetics of immunity and cancer, genetic technology in medicine and ethical and social issues related to medical genetics.

PATH5066.title: Directed Readings
PATH5066.description: This course provides an opportunity for individual students to study, in depth, a subject related to pathology that isn’t offered as a formal course at Dalhousie. A supervisor is chosen for each student, based on his/her expertise and the topic of interest. The student and supervisor meet regularly to discuss assigned readings. The student must prepare a written paper or oral presentation to the Department each term.

PATH5067.title: Directed Readings
PATH5067.description: This course provides an opportunity for individual students to study, in depth, a subject related to pathology that isn’t offered as a formal course at Dalhousie. A supervisor is chosen for each student, based on his/her expertise and the topic of interest. The student and supervisor meet regularly to discuss assigned readings. The student must prepare a written paper or oral presentation to the Department each term.

PATH5068.title: Directed Readings
PATH5068.description: This course provides an opportunity for individual students to study, in depth, a subject related to pathology that isn’t offered as a formal course at Dalhousie. A supervisor is chosen for each student, based on his/her expertise and the topic of interest. The student and supervisor meet regularly to discuss assigned readings. The student must prepare a written paper or oral presentation to the Department each term.

PATH5091.title: Pathol Research Seminar Series
PATH5091.description: The objectives of this course are: 1) to provide a forum for graduate students to develop skills at presenting seminars; 2) to provide constructive evaluation of their research; and 3) to promote interaction between students and faculty.

PATH5835.title: HG Adv Topics
PATH5835.description: An Advanced core course for MSc and PhD students in Human Genetics and Genomics, Pathology, graduate students with a special interest in human genetics, and CCMG fellows. Topics include Cell division and chromatin behaviour; chromosomal structural abnormalities and reproductive consequences; Developmental genetics; Cancer genetics; Bayesian Risk calculations; Linkage, segregation, and association analysis; non-mendelian genetics epigenetics and imprinting; Sequencing and new technology platforms and associated analysis tools; Variant interpretation; and Cytogenetics.

Carleton COLLABORATIVE HEALTH EDUC BLDG C220

PATH9416.title: PhD Research Proposal
PATH9416.description:
All MSc students want to reclassify to PhD program need to write 5 page Research proposal which is evaluated by their committee members to assess if it is acceptable for a PhD Thesis.
All PhD students directly admitted into the PhD program are also required to write 5 page research proposal as part of their PhD program.

PERF1001.title: Writing about Music
PERF1001.description: This course is an introduction to the academic study of music. It is designed to help students develop effective research and writing skills and to familiarize them with the sources, methods, repertories, and debates that have shaped music history and scholarship. Students will develop critical listening and analytical skills, will be challenged to consider music from a variety of perspectives, will become familiar with a number of standard works from various repertories, and will engage in the issues and debates surrounding various musical cultures.

PERF1002.title: Watching Performance
PERF1002.description: What is performance, and who counts as a performer? Why is performance one of the most ancient and durable aspects of human community and interaction? Why do we adore certain performers and despise others? How are performers and their choices shaped by their societies, and vice versa? This course will explore these questions by looking at some of the vital roles fulfilled by theatrical, musical, and cinematic performers in global societies, both ancient and modern. Via readings of articles and plays as well as in-class screenings of film and video performances, it will consider the performer's role in shaping, embodying, and questioning societies' conceptions of beauty, morality, religious faith, gender, race, ethnicity, social class, and more.

PERF2023.title: Basic Dance
PERF2023.description: This course will encourage students to develop skills, understandings and techniques in the basic aspects of jazz/ballet/and creative movement techniques. Development of confidence and expression is emphasized through understanding of the physical and expressive body, proper placement, dance history, class etiquette and dance vocabulary. This class is open to students with at least 3 years of recent dance training in such disciplines as ballet, modern or jazz techniques.

PERF2024.title: Elementary Dance
PERF2024.description: This dance course is an experiential studio class at an elementary level which allows dance students to maintain their training level in their dance technique while learning new elements and variations of techniques to supplement their training. This class is open to students at an elementary level and personal movement exploration is encouraged.

PERF2412.title: Language of Design
PERF2412.description: This course explores visual storytelling and ways of seeing within theatrical and performative contexts. Focusing on perception, visual composition, and narrative, students investigate how elements such as colour, form, texture, and space contribute to the creation of visual meaning and shape audience experience. Through lectures, discussion, and creative practice, the course introduces key principles of design language, visual analysis, and interpretation, encouraging critical observation and imaginative experimentation. Students will engage in translating conceptual ideas into visual form using a range of media and expressive techniques. The course is open to general BA students and is also a part of the Costume Studies and Stage Design & Technical Theatre Program.

PERF2451.title: Costume Design 1
PERF2451.description: In this course, the student will build on the foundation gained in THEA 2412 to research, conceptualize, and illustrate theoretical costume designs for theatre and other modes of performance. In addition, students will utilize their applied skills to better understand the integral role played by costume in staging a performance, in supporting an actor’s embodiment of character, and in diverse body representation. This course is part of the Costume Studies Program and is open to all theatre majors.

PERF2710.title: Stage Design 1
PERF2710.description: In this course, the student develops expertise in text analysis and communication specific to set design, building on the foundations learned in THEA 2412. Through applied projects, students will explore three-dimensional space development, sight lines, model building, and traditional hand drafting.

PERF2901.title: Dramaturgy
PERF2901.description: This course introduces students to the dramaturgical work of dramaturges and directors in the theatre. Students will learn skills including the presenting of research, the preparation of playtexts, the adapting of playtexts for new theatrical contexts, and the creation of theatrical seasons and programs.

PERF2902.title: Play Analysis for Directing
PERF2902.description: This course introduces students to the director’s process in analyzing a dramatic script for performance. Working with plays from a range of periods and genres, students will explore key theoretical approaches to directorial analysis, will learn the director’s core vocabulary, and will apply these discoveries to practical scene work.

PERF3023.title: Intermediate Dance Skills
PERF3023.description: This dance course is an experiential studio class at an intermediate level, which allows dance students to maintain their training level in their dance technique while learning new elements and variations of techniques to supplement their training. This class is open to students at an intermediate level and personal movement exploration is encouraged.

PERF3408.title: Aesthetics of Costume Ornament
PERF3408.description: This course will explore the historical relevance and versatility of traditional ornamentation and embellishment methods as well as non-traditional methods of textile manipulation. Utilizing the techniques studied and applied in class, students will gain the ability to re-create and re-interpret ornamentation and methods of embellishing and explore its potential application in costume production. Multiple techniques will be examined through a variety of materials and specialized construction techniques including the interaction of surface design and 3-D form. Students will be required to engage with both machine and hand sewing to fully execute the manipulation techniques.

PERF3830.title: Dance and Movement Composition
PERF3830.description: Dance composition is the art of designing and creating a dance. In this course, students will engage in the practical application of dance techniques to create and choreograph performance pieces. The course explores the structuring of ideas and exercises focusing on time, space, and energy.

PERF4250.title: Thtr & Music Entrepreneurship
PERF4250.description: A business course designed for those interested in arts-led entrepreneurial ventures and self-producing theatre, music and film events for public platforms. It is aimed at developing the preparatory skill set needed for entrepreneurial ventures, which can feature creative products, services, and performances. Content will focus on an arts-led approach and how this can define entrepreneurial ventures, operations, and engagement with audiences and customers. Product benefits, customer groups, promotion, branding, distribution, financial and legal concepts, and digital platforms will be examined through the creative arts lens. Finally, audience-building strategies for those leading small performing arts organizations will be explored.

PERI5110.title: Clinical Periodontics I
PERI5110.description: Presented in three didactic, laboratory and clinical modules, this course offers students basic and fundamental skills and knowledge required in treating patients who present with various forms of periodontal disease and those in need of dental implants.

PERI5120.title: Evidence-Based Dent & Biostat
PERI5120.description: This course will outline basic research designs and levels of clinical evidence. The dental clinical epidemiology component of this course will cover the scientific basis for clinical decision making in prognosis, causation, diagnosis, and therapy according to the principles of evidence-based healthcare. Examples from the dental literature are used to illustrate these concepts and their practical application. The Biostatistics section is designed to provide graduate students with a basic understanding of the statistical methods used for data analysis and literature interpretation.

PERI6110.title: Clinical Periodontics II
PERI6110.description: A continuum of Clinical Periodontics I, this course exposes students to more complex cases requiring more advanced treatment modalities. An evidence-based approach to treatment is emphasized throughout the course. Students are expected to document their cases for presentation and discussion.

PERI7110.title: Clinical Periodontics III
PERI7110.description: A continuum of Clinical Periodontics I and II, this course exposes students to more complex cases requiring more advanced treatment modalities. An evidence-based approach to treatment is emphasized throughout the course. Students are expected to document their cases for presentation and discussion.

PERI7130.title: Graduate Dentistry Seminars
PERI7130.description: This course covers many aspects of speciality practice not covered in other required courses. Students will present clinical cases they treated in the clinic according to the format established by the Royal College of Dentists of Canada.

PERI7140.title: Hospital Rotation, Grad Dent.
PERI7140.description: This course focuses on management of the sedated patient and medical emergencies. Residents will be exposed to conscious sedation methods including anxiolysis through the use of nitrous oxide, oral sedation and single drug IV sedation; and participate in hospital rotations involving patients with a variety of medical disorders.

PERI7150.title: Lit Review in Periodontics
PERI7150.description: Taught in a seminar format, this course exposes students to contemporary periodontal and dental implant literature, drawn from various peer-reviewed journals. Students are expected to read and critique the assigned papers and to be able to convey their findings.

PERI7170.title: Research Practicum, Grad Dent.
PERI7170.description: The course is designed to enhance the student’s critical analysis and presentation skills and expose students to research methodologies. Students will work directly with a faculty advisor in developing a research project, carrying out the research and preparing a presentation for a scientific audience and a manuscript for publication based on their completed research.

PERI9000.title: Masters Thesis
PERI9000.description:
The course is designed to enhance the student’s critical analysis and presentation skills and expose students to
research methodologies. Students will work directly with a faculty advisor in developing a research project,
carrying out the research and prepare and defend a thesis in accordance with FGS guidance for the degree of MSc.

PHAC1471.title: Pharmacology for Pharmacy
PHAC1471.description: Part one of a two semester course providing an introduction to Pharmacology, emphasizing basic mechanisms of drug action and principals of drug-receptor interactions, pharmacokinetics, and drug metabolism.

PHAC1472.title: Pharmacology for Pharmacy
PHAC1472.description: Part two of a two semester course providing an introduction to Pharmacology, emphasizing basic mechanisms of drug action and principals of drug-receptor interactions, pharmacokinetics, and drug metabolism.

PHAC3000.title: Experiential Learning in PHAC
PHAC3000.description: This one semester course is intended to introduce students to outside-the-classroom learning experiences.  Students will work closely with a supervisor to learn laboratory skills and expand their knowledge in Pharmacology.  Course structure will vary, depending on the nature of the experience.

PHAC3030.title: The Drugs Around Us
PHAC3030.description:
Using examples of drugs found in our
environment and daily lives, this course
will discuss subjects including drug
regulations, how drugs affect us and
modify our body, foods that are
addictive; drugs in products you wouldn't
suspect as well as the treacherous effects
of common medications and
environmental toxins.

PHAC3333.title: Pharm Medicinal Plants
PHAC3333.description: Natural products remain an important source for the development of new therapeutics. The course explores the uses of plants, herbs and fungi as medicine, ranging from traditional approaches for treating ailments to modern pharmaceuticals.

PHAC4000.title: Dir Res in Pharmacology
PHAC4000.description: This course is intended to introduce students to academic research in a laboratory environment. Students will work closely with a supervisor to develop a research question and project proposal to address this question. Students will learn laboratory skills and expand their knowledge in Pharmacology.  It is expected that students will take 4000 & 4100 consecutively in Fall & Winter terms of the same academic year, unless otherwise agreed upon with the student, coordinator and supervisor.

PHAC4100.title: Dir Res in Pharmacology
PHAC4100.description: This course is intended to introduce students to academic research in a laboratory environment. Students will work closely with a supervisor to develop a research question and project proposal to address this question. Students will learn laboratory skills and expand their knowledge in Pharmacology.  It is expected that students will take 4000 & 4100 consecutively in Fall & Winter terms of the same academic year, unless otherwise agreed upon with the student, coordinator and supervisor.

PHAC4403.title: Systems Pharmacology I
PHAC4403.description: This course introduces pharmacology, the study of the interactions of drugs with the human body. Topics include drug receptors, drug metabolism, and drug distribution. Drugs acting on the autonomic nervous system, skeletal muscle, cardiovascular system, antimicrobial medications, plus anti-cancer drugs will be discussed. Content experts in pharmacology present different topics.

PHAC4409.title: Systems Pharmacology II
PHAC4409.description: This course is designed to complement Pharmacology I. It covers drug classes acting on various human body systems with emphasis on basic principles, mechanism of the drug action, therapeutic indications and adverse drug reactions. Topics include drugs acting on the central nervous system, drugs of abuse, local and general anesthetics, drugs acting on various endocrine glands, reproductive, immune, gastrointestinal and respiratory systems, anticancer drugs and drugs used in selected populations.

PHAC5405.title: Advanced Pharmacology
PHAC5405.description: Pharmacology employs a wide variety of experimental approaches to study drug action at the molecular, cellular, tissue, organ, and organism levels. This course describes the techniques used to develop safe and effective compounds and biologics with the appropriate pharmacokinetics properties for the treatment of a wide array of diseases. Students will first receive training in experimental design. This will be followed by a description of how drug targets have been identified for approved therapeutics. Students will then be introduced to the use of human stem cells and animal disease models for drug screening. Next, the students will receive training in drug absorption, distribution, metabolism, and elimination. Students will then learn about recent innovations in biologically based therapeutics and nanomedicine. Lastly, they will be taught how bioinformatics can be used to identify new drug targets and develop genetically based models to predict the human safety and efficacy of therapeutics that activate or inhibit them.

PHAC5406.title: Systems Pharmacology I
PHAC5406.description: This course introduces pharmacology, the study of the interactions of drugs with the human body. Topics include drug receptors, drug metabolism, and drug distribution. Drugs acting on the autonomic nervous system, skeletal muscle, cardiovascular system, antimicrobial medications, plus anti-cancer drugs will be discussed. Content experts in pharmacology present different topics.

PHAC5507.title: Pharmacology Practice Teaching
PHAC5507.description: This course is to provide Pharmacology Ph.D. students with a useful pedagogical knowledge base with an aim to develop a University level course. Specific emphasis will be on theoretical design, curriculum development and developing an appropriate examination platform consistent with the teaching modality. Practical development of a lecture and/or lecture series will be emphasized.

PHAC5508.title: PHAC MSc Seminar
PHAC5508.description: A mandatory course for all trainees in the Pharmacology graduate program. Satisfactory performance in the course components is required throughout the degree program for the student to be receive a passing grade in their final year. There are three components to the course: 1. The Pharmacology Departmental Seminar Series. Seminars are typically held weekly during the fall and winter terms and attendance is mandatory for all trainees in the Department of Pharmacology. Speakers come from a variety of backgrounds including academia, industry, and government. Students are often given the opportunity to meet informally with guest speakers. 2. Presentation of research seminars and attendance of Pharmacology Graduate Student Research Days. Typically research days are held annually in the fall (PhD) and winter (MSc) terms. While presentation is only required at the event linked to the trainee’s degree program, attendance is mandatory for both annual research days. Each trainee seminar is assessed by attending Faculty who provide oral and written feedback on the quality and content of their presentation. 3. Pharmacology Trainee Defences. Trainees must attend the graduate student defences presented in the Department of Pharmacology. These occur throughout the academic year on an ad hoc basis. NOTE: Course Details listed here also apply to PHAC 5509 (PhD)

PHAC5509.title: Phac Graduate Seminar (PhD)
PHAC5509.description: A mandatory course for all trainees in the Pharmacology graduate program. Satisfactory performance in the course components is required throughout the degree program for the student to be receive a passing grade in their final year. There are three components to the course: 1. The Pharmacology Departmental Seminar Series. Seminars are typically held weekly during the fall and winter terms and attendance is mandatory for all trainees in the Department of Pharmacology. Speakers come from a variety of backgrounds including academia, industry, and government. Students are often given the opportunity to meet informally with guest speakers. 2. Presentation of research seminars and attendance of Pharmacology Graduate Student Research Days. Typically research days are held annually in the fall (PhD) and winter (MSc) terms. While presentation is only required at the event linked to the trainee’s degree program, attendance is mandatory for both annual research days. Each trainee seminar is assessed by attending Faculty who provide oral and written feedback on the quality and content of their presentation. 3. Pharmacology Trainee Defences. Trainees must attend the graduate student defences presented in the Department of Pharmacology. These occur throughout the academic year on an ad hoc basis. NOTE: Course Details listed here also apply to PHAC 5508 (MSc)

PHAC5626.title: Special Topics in Pharmacology
PHAC5626.description: Students interested in topics not covered in formal courses may ask the department for special courses to meet their needs. The fields in which the department can offer instruction are reflected in the list of faculty research areas. Since different subjects may be covered each year, each course in the series has a separate number.

PHAC6319.title: Pharm Sci, Law and Policy
PHAC6319.description: This course provides students with a unique opportunity to learn about pharmaceutical policy challenges in an interdisciplinary environment. Open to students from the Faculty of Medicine, the course is co-located with a course offered to JD and LLM students from the Schulich School of Law, and will introduce students to the regulatory systems in place to govern pharmaceutical drugs and survey a number of ‘hot topics’ in the field, from national pharma-care, high-priced drugs for orphan diseases, and the opioid crisis, to legalizing cannabis. The course will also include guest lectures from experts in pharmaceutical sciences and key government agencies. Students will also learn new research and writing skills relevant to pharmaceutical science, law, and public policy.

PHAR1011.title: Critical Appraisal Series 1
PHAR1011.description: This course serves as the introduction to the Critical Appraisal Series (CAS) courses, exploring the foundational concepts of evidence-based practice, critical appraisal, and critical thinking as core principles in pharmacy education and practice. Students learn to evaluate and strategically utilize credible primary, secondary, and tertiary drug and health information resources—including key texts, bibliographic databases, journals, and other tools—as an integral component of patient care.

PHAR1040.title: Pharmaceutical Sciences
PHAR1040.description: This lecture-based course is comprised of three core pharmaceutical science subject areas: medicinal chemistry, pharmaceutics and biopharmaceutics and pharmacokinetics that will be taught concurrently. The course will provide students with a strong foundational knowledge in the core pharmaceutical sciences, which will support further integrated learning and application of pharmaceutical sciences principles as it relates to therapeutic topics and practical experience training during the remainder of the curriculum.

PHAR1051.title: Integrated PBL 1
PHAR1051.description: Integrated PBL 1, is the introductory Problem-based (PBL) learning course and the first of 6 PBL courses in the curriculum. Students will learn to use the pharmacy specific problem-solving process and will be introduced to lab values and physical assessment.  In the nutrition portion of the course, students will learn about nutritional needs of healthy clients and special populations. The roles, the daily requirements and sources of various vitamins, and pathological consequences of dietary deficiencies will be addressed. Special nutritional challenges in pregnancy, infancy, elderly, and grave illness will be examined. In the Eye and Ear portion, students learn the medicinal chemistry, pharmaceutics, biopharmaceutics and pharmacokinetics, and pharmacology, as well as the pathophysiology and pharmacotherapeutic principles pertaining to the problems and products discussed.  Common problems of the eye and ear, including those of an infectious and non-infectious nature will be examined. Students will apply cumulative knowledge to a complex patient case.

PHAR1052.title: Integrated PBL 2
PHAR1052.description: Integrated PBL 2 deals with common dermatological problems seen by pharmacists and the management of these problems. Students will learn about non-infectious respiratory complaints and gastrointestinal ailments and their management. Students will learn the medicinal chemistry, pharmaceutics, biopharmaceutics and pharmacokinetics, and pharmacology, as well as the pathophysiology and pharmacotherapeutic principles pertaining to the problems and products discussed. Students will apply cumulative knowledge to a complex patient case.

PHAR1061.title: Social Behaviour and Administr
PHAR1061.description: This course is the first course in a series that focus on the social, behavioural, and administrative responsibilities of a pharmacist. Each course will include learning about the principles of professionalism, ethics, and leadership. In this course students will learn about the Canadian Health Care System, global health and the history of pharmacy.

PHAR1062.title: Social Behaviour and Administr
PHAR1062.description: This course is the second course in a series that focus on the social, behavioural, and administrative responsibilities of a pharmacist. Each course will include learning about the principles of professionalism, ethics, and leadership. During this course, students will cover topics including cultural competency and diversity, approaches to modern medicine and pharmacotherapy, pharmacy law, and regulation of the profession.

PHAR1073.title: Skills Lab 1
PHAR1073.description: Skills Lab 1 is the first of 8 skills lab courses in the curriculum.  Students will explore the legal, ethical and practical aspects of pharmacy practice and discuss safe and effective practices within pharmacy workflow.  Students will learn fundamental frameworks and skills necessary for effective communication in pharmacy practice, including patient interviewing and over-the-counter medication consultations.  Students will learn and demonstrate proficiency in Medical Terminology.

PHAR1074.title: Skills Lab 2
PHAR1074.description: In this course students will learn the fundamentals of the Pharmacist’s Patient Care Process and further develop communication skills to effectively assess and communicate with patients. Students will have the opportunity to apply therapeutic content learning in PBL to various consultations including new prescription consultations. Students will be introduced to basic concepts of patient assessment, physical assessment and clinical documentation. Students will assess, identify and manage common drug therapy problems in patient encounters related to OTC consultations, prescription therapy and drug interactions. Students will be introduced to patient monitoring consultations.

PHAR1075.title: Skills Lab 3
PHAR1075.description: In this course students will learn the fundamentals of pharmacy calculations and fundamental methods of compounding for day-to-day pharmacy practice. Students will explore compounding literature in order to gain skills in researching formulas and ingredient information.
